Award 2 marks for ONE value:
• Fynbos is unique to this region and tourists are drawn to see the fynbos.
• As it is special to this WHS, it will be protected and tourists can be sure that it will continue to exist. It is a draw card for tourists to the area.
• Different types of tourists will be attracted to this biome.
• It can generate income for businesses operating in and around the area.

subQuestions.questionText: A fire destroyed a small part on the edge of Table Mountain National Park, one of the thirteen protected area clusters included on the World Heritage list and one of the world's greatest biodiversity 'hotspots'. In a paragraph, discuss THREE threats of uncontrolled fires as a result of irresponsible tourist behaviour in the area.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each threat (max 6 marks):
• Fires threaten the fynbos. The loss of fynbos will have a negative impact on tourism as many tourists will no longer be attracted to the area.
• Fires can destroy the nature trails, tourism infrastructure and neighbouring communities in this area.
• Irresponsible tourist behaviour can lead to loss of life.
• As it takes many months to regrow, tourists will not be able to visit this area. This will lead to a loss of income.
• Air quality is negatively affected.
• Destruction of vegetation can lead to erosion.

subQuestions.questionText: Study the image on gearing up for growth at Meetings Africa 2023. Name the marketing organisation responsible for hosting Meetings Africa 2023. (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer (2 marks): South African Tourism / SATourism

NOTE: Do not accept SAT.

subQuestions.questionText: Identify ONE type of tourist that will be attracted to this event.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for any ONE:
• Meetings, Incentive, Conferences and Exhibitions tourists / MICE tourists
• MESE (Meetings, Exhibitions and Special Events)
• Business tourists
• Education tourists
• Bleisure tourist

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO other international travel trade shows where South Africa is marketed.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark each (2 marks):
• ITB Berlin
• World Travel Market / WTM

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss TWO ways in which international travel trade shows can position South Africa as a destination of choice.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each way (max 4 marks):
• International travel trade shows will increase networking opportunities.
• It will create awareness of South Africa as a travel destination.
• Internationally South Africa will be seen as a welcoming host and a great value for money destination.
• South Africa will be considered as a host country for other international events.
• A positive experience can lead to positive publicity for South Africa.
• Exhibitors at international travel trade shows will be exposed to all South Africa has to offer, which will persuade them to visit the country.
• International travel trade shows will encourage investment opportunities for the country.

subQuestions.questionText: A uniform contributes to the professional image of an airline. Discuss TWO ways in which the correct manner in which employees wear a uniform contributes to the professional image of an airline. (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each way (max 4 marks):
• While in uniform, employees may not display any inappropriate behaviour that will bring an airline into disrepute.
• It creates a sense of pride.
• The company ensures that the employees wear clothes that suit the line of work (location and occupation).
• The design of the uniform is appropriate for the different cultures, religions or age groups.
• Uniforms are elegant, sophisticated and represent the airline.

subQuestions.questionText: Complete the sentence below. The staff responsible for the safety of passengers onboard the aircraft is the ...
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for any ONE:
• Cabin crew
• Flight attendant
• Pilot
• First officer

subQuestions.questionText: The cabin crew of an airline has many responsibilities. Give ONE condition as part of the airline's code of conduct on the following: Punctuality.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE condition (cabin crew must):
• Report for duty on time.
• Be able to manage their time.
• Not be late as it will have an effect on the rest of the airline operation.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE condition as part of the airline's code of conduct on the following: Treatment of passengers.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE condition:
• The crew members may not be rude to passengers.
• Passengers should always be treated with respect.
• Crew members should not become too familiar with passengers.
• Crew must be firm towards unruly passengers who threaten the safety of other passengers.

NOTE: Accept examples of the treatment of passengers.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word for the definition below. Using resources in a way that meets the needs of current generations without compromising the needs of future generations.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer (2 marks): Sustainability

NOTE: Do not accept the words 'sustainable tourism'.

subQuestions.questionText: Hotel groups can reduce their impact on the environment in different ways. Discuss TWO ways how the hotel can manage the following sustainable practice to reduce their impact on the environment: Water management.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each way (max 4 marks):
• Capture and harvest rainwater in tanks.
• Dual-flush toilets in the bathrooms.
• Low flow shower heads in the showers.
• Reuse grey water.
• Use energy efficient appliances such as dishwashers and washing machines.
• Re-use bath towels.

NOTE: Accept examples of water management practices.

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss TWO ways how the hotel can manage the following sustainable practice to reduce their impact on the environment: Energy management.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each way (max 4 marks):
• The use of alternative energy sources and devices.
• The use of trees and plants to create cool areas for guests to relax.
• The use of electronic key cards that regulates electricity usage in the room.
• Using energy saving light bulbs.
• Use local products and services to save on fuel costs.
• Encourage tourists to use bicycles when exploring surrounding areas.
• The use of large windows and skylights to allow for natural light during the day.
• Use energy efficient appliances such as dishwashers, washing machines and cooling systems.

NOTE: Accept examples of energy management practices.

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss THREE positive impacts of tourism on the global economy.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each positive impact (max 6 marks):
• Tourism can generate job opportunities across all sectors.
• Tourism generates income and it contributes to the GDP.
• Tourism assists in the development of new infrastructure.
• Maintaining and improving the existing infrastructure.
• It can drive social and economic development.
• Tourism can create entrepreneurial opportunities in many sectors in the economy.
• Tourism can set the multiplier effect into motion.
• Tourism business can adopt sustainable practices leading to a growth in the global economy.

subQuestions.questionText: Many tourism businesses are NOT in favour of using the Weeva digital system as it may expose their carbon footprint. Suggest TWO ways in which you would encourage these businesses to make use of the Weeva digital system and thereby enjoy the benefits of reduced environmental impacts.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each way (max 4 marks):
• If a business is aware of its carbon footprint, solutions can be found to lessen the impact on the environment.
• The businesses will become more serious about sustainability and will make the effort to change their operations thereby reducing the impact on the environment.
• The business may qualify for certification as a green business that will give them the competitive edge.
• The business will attract environmentally conscious tourists.
• Facilitate collaboration amongst tourism businesses to share best practices.
• Businesses must be given a trial period to test and integrate the Weeva system.

subQuestions.questionText: Read the information about the 2026 FIFA World Cup to be held in North America (hosted jointly by the USA, Canada and Mexico). Give ONE reason why the extract refers to a continent and not to a single country.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer (2 marks): The extract refers to a continent as the event will jointly be hosted by three countries on the same continent, i.e. North America.

subQuestions.questionText: Identify TWO reasons why the 2026 FIFA World Cup will be unique.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each reason (max 4 marks):
• It will be the first time that three countries jointly host the event.
• It will be the first time that 48 teams will be competing.

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO reasons why the 2026 FIFA World Cup is considered a global event.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each reason (max 4 marks):
• It attracts spectators and participants from across the globe.
• The event will have a positive economic impact on all three host countries.
• It will attract interest from the media, sponsors and support staff travelling with all teams.
• The event can reach millions of people through the broadcasting of the event worldwide.

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss ONE positive impact the FIFA World Cup will have on the economy of the North American continent.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE positive impact:
• More visitors will visit the countries.
• Foreign exchange will be generated and shared by all countries.
• More products and services will be needed.
• Jobs / entrepreneurial opportunities will be created.
• Increase in GDP for all host nations.
• Exposure and publicity of the countries will result in repeat visits.
• The multiplier effect will be put into motion.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the concept multiple-entry visa.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks:
• A multiple-entry visa will allow tourists to visit the three countries more than once, whilst the visa is valid.
• They will only need to apply for one visa to enter three countries.

subQuestions.questionText: Study the information on more visitors to the Kruger National Park. Identify, from graph A, the core market with the lowest visitor numbers. (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer (2 marks): United States / USA / United States of America

NOTE: Accept the name of the market only.

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to graph B. Discuss ONE reason why both Mpumalanga and Limpopo are considered two of the top three provinces for domestic visitors to the Kruger National Park. (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE reason:
• The KNP is located within the borders of Mpumalanga and Limpopo.
• It is in close proximity to the park.
• It is the main attraction in both provinces.
• People can enter the KNP from one province and leave the park through the other province.

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the information in C. Give ONE reason why the recorded visitor numbers are compared to the 2019 season and not to the 2020/2021 season.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE reason:
• It is more realistic to compare the numbers from 2018/2019 as these years reflect pre-Covid-19 visitor numbers.
• The visitor numbers for the 2020/2021 season were not realistic because of the Covid-19 pandemic.

subQuestions.questionText: Study the infographic 'Tourism businesses take note - numbers do not lie', which analyses customer services and experiences. Explain TWO reasons why the findings above are important to tourism businesses. (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for each reason (max 4 marks):
• The findings are valuable to all tourism businesses to retain its customer base.
• The findings will show the company's weaknesses and serve as a guide for the business to develop its plan of action.
• The findings will show the company where it can improve its level of service.
• The findings will result in increased profitability.

NOTE: Accept examples from the infographic.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the meaning of the finding, 'It takes 12 positive experiences to make up for one negative one.' (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks:
• It means that it is much harder to win back a customer as it will take many attempts to do so.
• These attempts will place extra strain on the company's financial resources.
• Bad service can lead to a loss of customers. It will take time and effort to win back a customer.
• A negative experience may result in the spreading of negative word of mouth, which can cost the company its reputation.

subQuestions.questionText: Study the cartoon of a disappointed customer complaining about poor service. State ONE way in which management could respond appropriately to the customer. (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE way:
• Apologise to the customer for the poor service and excuses.
• Reassure the customer of his/her value to the business.
• Assure the customer that it will not happen again.

subQuestions.questionText: Recommend ONE strategy a company can use to win back the customer's loyalty. (Refer to the source/image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ONE strategy:
• The company can offer a form of compensation to the customer.
• A manager can follow up with a personal call to the customer and apologise on behalf of the company.
• The company can ask the customer to suggest ways on how to win back their loyalty.
